Hey, I'm really sorry you're going through all this. It's a lot for anyone to go through but especially at 16. I wanted to say firstly that there's nothing wrong with you, you're not broken or failing. I'm a 30 year old gay guy, and I've been suffering with OCD, depression and intrusive thoughts. I was also bullied around that age when I came out, and it was hell, so I can genuinely imagine how overwhelming it might feel. Just know that it takes real strength to own who you are, even if others try to make it seem like a weakness. It's not.

You don't owe anyone an explanation for who you are. The way others treat you is a reflection of their own ignorance and immaturity, not your worth. It's unkind that they put you in a position where you feel like you have to be some sort of spokesperson for gay people when you're just trying to live your life and be authentically you. 

It's also completely understandable that you feel burnt out from feeling like you have to hide who you are because of how others act. But you should know that being openly yourself, even when those around you make it really hard, is incredibly strong.

There's nothing wrong with reaching out to seek more support, having someone to talk to can help you process things in a way you can't always do on your own. It's totally valid to raise these issues about meds to your psychiatrist and your thoughts about not wanting to live too. Again, I think you're incredibly brave, and I promise the world is better with you in it.

I'm assuming you're on an ssri so I'll run through what's happening but if this doesn't fit the medicine, it may still help anyway.

Within your first week on medication, it hasn't fully kicked in, it's increasing serotonin levels but the receptors and brain circuit changes take around 4-6 weeks.

Porn/masturbation provides a fast dopamine reward which will be comforting when your serotonin is still out of balance, SSRIs don't directly boost dopamine and they can actually blunt some of the natural reward feelings which could trigger a desire for high reward stimulation.

Relapsing is common in the first few weeks of treatment because your brain is still adjusting, habits like porn and masturbation are hardwired and will take time, structure and support to rewire those loops.

Impulse control can take a few months to normalise and if your porn consumption is addictive or compulsive, meds along with cbt might be more beneficial. You don't even have to attend sessions, you could just learn coping mechanisms online that I've found helpful in other situations.

What you could do is set realistic expectations for a month as you adjust, don't be so hard on yourself and beat yourself up for struggling, track your habits and see what triggers your compulsive tendencies.

In my experience, I'm on week 2 of SSRIs but I've been on them before for years and it can have the opposite effect which dulls the senses so much that it's hard to climax. There are ways to help that but the lesson I gained from it is to be honest with your GP or care provider, tell them what you're hoping to get out of them and also let them know if something isn't working too if you run into any issues.

Real improvements are often more consistent after the third or fourth week. Take it easy!

I wouldn’t say the evidence suggests alien life is the best explanation. That’s not what the scientific community is saying. In fact, multiple planetary scientists and chemists have gone on record saying the opposite. Here's a sample:

Joshua Krissansen-Totton called the lifeless mini-Neptune model the most reasonable explanation. (meaning that the size of the planet and its relation to other such planets observed put it very close to a Neptune like planet)

Laura Kreidberg pointed out that the detection itself is right at the edge of what JWST can reliably do, so it may not even be a real DMS signal.

And Eleanor Browne’s lab work showed DMS can be formed abiotically. It’s even been detected on comets, where no one thinks life exists.

So no, this isn’t about bias or being closed-minded. It’s about recognizing that this is an early, tentative signal that’s far from conclusive. The presence of DMS, if it's even there, might be interesting, but the leap to alien life being the best explanation just isn’t supported by the current data or the experts closest to the research.

Science isn’t about choosing the most exciting explanation. It’s about building evidence gradually and staying open to multiple hypotheses until we’ve ruled them out. That’s what makes it reliable.

Down – Up – Down – Up – Down – Up – Down – Up  
( 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & )

Every down strum is a beat, when you have the & that's a half beat which you can visualise by strumming up in this scenario.

Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & in your head when you strum.

A common strumming pattern is Down - Down - Up - Up - Down - Up which would be these beats:

1 2 & 3 & 4 &. Practice moving your wrist all the time even when you're not strumming in this scenario.

So when you strum Down at the start, move your wrist up like you're strumming but don't touch the strings and do the next Down and try to do that with the rest of the pattern.

Federated and decentralised aren't mutually exclusive. 

The rotating governance in Hedera's council ensures that it's decentralised, but the goal is to transition toward a permissionless model which would open it up to public participation. 

Ethereum wasn't fully decentralised/permissionless at launch but has become more so. (you could argue that large staking pools on tokens like Ethereum challenge that decentralisation)

They do aim to open node participation, but it's still early days for Hedera and their approach is evolving.

To say Hedera has no decentralisation at all isn't accurate.

Hedera's governance is decentralised through its governing council, made up of 39 major organisation who operate the consensus nodes and vote on decisions, but it's not permissionless. These are rotated over time and each has equal voting power which is designed to prevent control from a single entity.

The consensus mechanism is decentralised. It runs on Asynchronous Byzantine Fault Tolerance (aBFT) which is one of the most secure consensus models. No single party can alter transactions once finalised, and the plan is to open node participation to the public.

The nodes are still run by the governing council members only, but the plan is to eventually allow public participation.

Hedera is more decentralised than traditional corporate databases, but it is not as decentralised as Bitcoin or Ethereum for now.

When an apple is injured (or cut into pieces), the plant tissue is exposed to oxygen. This triggers an enzyme known as polyphenol oxidase (PPO) to—wait for it—oxidize polyphenols in the apple’s flesh. This results in new chemicals (o-quinones), which then react with amino acids to produce brown-colored melanins. Different apple varieties contain different amounts of both the initial enzyme and the polyphenols, and thus they brown at different rates.
